statement: The table shows a school club's planned budget for the year. $$\begin{array}{l|r} \text{Item} & \text{Amount} \\ \hline \text{Supplies} & \$400 \\ \text{Travel} & \$900 \\ \text{Food} & \$300 \\ \text{Prizes} & \$400 \end{array}$$ The club decides to increase the amount for Supplies by $30\%$ and keep every other amount the same. By what percent does the total budget increase?

choices.misconception: I thought raising one item by 30 percent raises the whole budget by 30 percent.
I found that Supplies is 400 out of 2,000, or 20 percent of the budget, and gave that share instead of the increase.
I spread the 30 percent evenly across the 4 items, $30\% \div 4 = 7.5\%$, even though the items have different amounts.

hints: Find the total budget and the dollar amount of the increase.
The total is $\$2{,}000$, and $30\%$ of the $\$400$ for Supplies is $\$120$.
The increase as a percent of the total is $\frac{120}{2{,}000}$.

solutions.reliable: The total budget is $400 + 900 + 300 + 400 = 2{,}000$ dollars. Supplies rises by $0.30 \cdot 400 = 120$ dollars, and nothing else changes, so the total rises by $120$ dollars. As a percent of the original total, that is $\frac{120}{2{,}000} = 0.06$, or $6\%$.
solutions.elegant: Supplies is $\frac{400}{2{,}000} = 20\%$ of the budget. Raising $20\%$ of the budget by $30\%$ raises the whole by $0.20 \cdot 30\% = 6\%$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
